analysisSummary: Mechanic confirmed by execution, but no fund-loss impact: BENCH has no redemption path, leaveStaking requires user.amount, and the only effect is receipt-token dilution, which the program explicitly excludes. PoC proves 0 VVS extraction.
counterEvidence: Workbench.sol:11-35 exposes only owner-gated mint/burn/safeVVSTransfer and no holder redemption; Craftsman.sol:284-302 leaveStaking requires user.amount>=_amount; poc testEmergencyWithdrawKeepsBenchButExtractsNothing passes (retained BENCH extracts 0 VVS). Program excludes rewards dilution and lists VVS-Bench out of scope.

analysisSummary: Mechanic confirmed by execution, but only with a hook token in an owner-added pool: the control test with a plain ERC20 pays exactly pending. Precondition is excluded by two program rules and the CEI pattern is SlowMist N9.
counterEvidence: Craftsman.sol:220-240 payment-before-transfer ordering is real, but poc testPlainLpDepositPaysExactlyPending proves exact payment with a plain ERC20; hook-token double-pay (testHookLpDepositDoublePaysPending) requires an owner-added pool (Craftsman.sol:114 add onlyOwner). Program excludes privileged-address attacks and third-party malicious pools; SlowMist N9 duplicates the CEI pattern; live BONUS_MULTIPLIER=0.

analysisSummary: Malleability is real in the deployed bytecode (no s-bound constant), but it yields no approval or funds for the attacker: the malleated signature authorizes the same spender/value. Worst case is griefing a victim permit tx (DoS, excluded). Canonical UniswapV2 behavior + SlowMist N5 duplicate.
counterEvidence: Pair permit reverts 'VVS: INVALID_SIGNATURE' on bad signatures (probe); malleated (v,s) still recovers the same owner for the same digest fields, so _approve(owner, spender, value) is unchanged; program excludes DoS and previously-known Ethereum/fork vulnerabilities; SlowMist N5 reported this mechanism.

analysisSummary: Separator is fixed at deploy as in canonical UniswapV2, but exploitation needs a hypothetical chain split preserving chainId and addresses. Not unequivocally executable; SlowMist N4 duplicate.
counterEvidence: DOMAIN_SEPARATOR recomputed exactly for chainId 25 (probe); no chain split exists; SlowMist N4 reported the identical mechanism and it was ignored; program requires unequivocally executable PoCs and excludes previously-known fork vulnerabilities.

analysisSummary: Overflow is arithmetically possible in the abstract but unreachable: balances are bounded by the CRO supply, orders of magnitude below 2^256, and every increment is backed by value or an existing balance. Repo file is not even the deployed code.
counterEvidence: Deployed WCRO totalSupply() == native balance == 6.84e26 wei, far below 2^256; WCRO.sol:20/56 increments are bounded by msg.value and prior balances; canonical WETH9 behavior, excluded as previously-known.

analysisSummary: Owner powers are real and sweeping, but every path requires the privileged owner EOA. The program excludes attacks requiring privileged addresses, and SlowMist N1/N10 already reported excessive authority.
counterEvidence: Craftsman.sol:104,114,130,156,324 all onlyOwner; migrator() == address(0) and BONUS_MULTIPLIER == 0 live (probes), so the two sharpest legs are inert; program out-of-scope list excludes privileged-address attacks; SlowMist N1/N10 duplicates.

analysisSummary: Accounting mismatch is real for fee-on-transfer tokens, but it is SlowMist N6 verbatim (ignored, team will not use deflationary tokens) and requires an owner-added pool with such a token.
counterEvidence: Craftsman.sol:114 add is onlyOwner; SlowMist N6 describes the identical deposit/withdraw mismatch; no live pool uses a fee-on-transfer token (all pools are VVS-LP/VVS); program excludes third-party malicious-pool preconditions.

analysisSummary: Donation dilutes per-share rewards, but the donor loses their own tokens to benefit all stakers pro-rata; there is no drain path and the impact is rewards dilution, explicitly excluded.
counterEvidence: Craftsman.sol:206 lpSupply is balance-based; donated LP has no corresponding user.amount and cannot be withdrawn by the donor except via a stake they do not hold; known MasterChef behavior, excluded as previously-known and as rewards dilution.

analysisSummary: Self-lock is real but self-inflicted and recoverable: the staker chose to transfer BENCH, and transferring it back restores the exit. No attacker involvement, no fund loss. PoC proves both the revert and the recovery.
counterEvidence: poc testBenchRequiredToLeaveStaking passes: leaveStaking reverts after BENCH transfer and succeeds after BENCH return; Craftsman.sol:299 bench.burn is the only blocker and BENCH is freely transferable.

analysisSummary: Division by zero needs the owner to zero all allocations (privileged, excluded); impact is a revert/DoS of reward updates, also excluded; stakes stay withdrawable via emergencyWithdraw which skips updatePool.
counterEvidence: Craftsman.sol:130 set is onlyOwner; Craftsman.sol:304-312 emergencyWithdraw does not call updatePool, so user funds remain exitable; program excludes DoS and privileged-address attacks.

analysisSummary: Catch-up calls are real but owner-only, and each call is capped by the 30%-community rule; no unprivileged path exists.
counterEvidence: VVSInitMintable.sol:27 distributeSupply is onlyOwner (via Craftsman.sol:324 onlyOwner); line 46 enforces communitySupplyPerYear >= 30% of SUPPLY_PER_YEAR per call; program excludes privileged-address attacks.

analysisSummary: All named shapes are canonical UniswapV2 behaviors, excluded as previously-known Ethereum/fork vulnerabilities; empty-pool shapes are separately excluded by name. No VVS-specific deviation was found in the probed surface; absence of source is a coverage limit, not evidence of a bug.
counterEvidence: Probes: router getAmountOut 997/1000 fee math, pair MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY 1000, CREATE2/init-hash reproduction, DOMAIN_SEPARATOR recomputation, renamed canonical revert strings; program out-of-scope list covers previously-known fork vulnerabilities and zero-share pools/vaults.
